l4_steps.name: Retrieve scheduled work orders for inbound aircraft
l4_steps.input: Published flight schedule and aircraft tail assignment from Amadeus SkyWORKS
l4_steps.output: Work pack listing all due scheduled tasks, AD compliance items, and component changes
l4_steps.kpi: Work pack issued ≥4 hours before estimated aircraft arrival
l4_steps.pain_point: Late schedule changes from network operations can invalidate pre-built work packs; AMOS work order generation requires manual re-trigger when tail swaps occur

l4_steps.name: Load MEL/CDL deferred defect carry-forwards
l4_steps.input: Open defect records from previous station's Electronic Technical Log
l4_steps.output: Annotated work pack with deferred items, MEL interval expiry dates, and required rectification actions
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of Category B/C MEL items captured before aircraft arrival; zero Category A items carried forward
l4_steps.pain_point: ETL records from outstations transmitted via ACARS can arrive incomplete; discrepancies between paper ATL and AMOS electronic record create compliance exposure

l4_steps.name: Confirm parts, tools, and crew availability
l4_steps.input: Work pack task list and station inventory snapshot from AMOS stores module
l4_steps.output: Resource-confirmed work pack or escalation to AOG desk for missing items
l4_steps.kpi: Resource confirmation completed ≥2 hours before arrival; parts availability ≥95% for scheduled tasks
l4_steps.pain_point: Station stock levels for consumables (O-rings, filters, fluids) are often below safety stock due to demand spikes; AMOS min/max reorder logic not consistently tuned per station size

l4_steps.name: Receive Electronic Technical Log from flight crew
l4_steps.input: Completed ETL entries from captain (defects, oil uptakes, cabin reports) transmitted via FliteDeck EFB
l4_steps.output: Acknowledged defect list with timestamp of handover; open items transferred to AMOS
l4_steps.kpi: ETL handover completed within 10 minutes of blocks-on; 100% of defects transferred to AMOS within 15 minutes
l4_steps.pain_point: EFB-to-MRO system integration gaps require manual re-keying of defects into AMOS at some stations, introducing transcription risk and adding 10–15 minutes to turnaround

l4_steps.name: Categorise open defects by MEL interval and severity
l4_steps.input: Defect entries from ETL handover; MEL/MMEL reference document in AMOS
l4_steps.output: Prioritised defect list: Category A (immediate), B (3 days), C (10 days), D (120 days)
l4_steps.kpi: Defect categorisation completed within 5 minutes of ETL receipt; zero mis-categorisations identified at next audit
l4_steps.pain_point: Engineers at outstations may lack current AMM/MEL revision; AMOS does not auto-flag MEL revision mismatches between aircraft effectivity and loaded document version

l4_steps.name: Assess Category A defects and trigger AOG response
l4_steps.input: Categorised defect list; FAR Part 43 and airline MOE airworthiness standards
l4_steps.output: AOG work order raised in AMOS with resource and parts requirements; MCC notified via ACARS/phone bridge
l4_steps.kpi: AOG notification to MCC within 5 minutes of Category A identification; AOG rectification plan confirmed within 30 minutes
l4_steps.pain_point: MCC visibility of real-time station technician availability is limited; AOG coordination relies on phone bridge rather than integrated workforce management, causing delays during high-disruption events

l4_steps.name: Perform exterior walkaround inspection per AMM 05-10
l4_steps.input: Approved work pack with transit check task cards; AMM Chapter 05-10 inspection criteria
l4_steps.output: Signed-off walkaround task card in AMOS; new defects raised as open items
l4_steps.kpi: Walkaround completed within 15 minutes of blocks-on; defect detection rate benchmarked against fleet average
l4_steps.pain_point: Short turnaround windows (25–45 min at focus cities) compress walkaround time; pressure to dispatch on-time can lead to incomplete checks — a known FAA audit finding category

l4_steps.name: Service aircraft fluids — fuel, engine oil, hydraulic, LOX
l4_steps.input: Fuel uplift order from flight dispatch (Jeppesen FliteDeck); oil consumption trend from CAMP
l4_steps.output: Fluid servicing task cards signed off; uplift quantities logged in AMOS and transmitted to fuel vendor
l4_steps.kpi: Engine oil consumption ≤0.3 qt/hr per engine; hydraulic fluid level within limits; LOX quantity per MEL minimum
l4_steps.pain_point: High oil consumption trending on CFM56-7B engines requires tracking against CAMP trend monitoring; deferred oil top-ups due to short turns inflate consumption variance and can trigger premature engine shop visit

l4_steps.name: Complete avionics and safety equipment functional checks
l4_steps.input: Transit check task card list; crew defect reports referencing avionics squawks
l4_steps.output: Signed-off avionics check records; unresolved items escalated to LAME for MEL assessment
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of safety-critical checks (fire detection, ELT, emergency lighting) signed off before departure; zero open avionics items departing without MEL disposition
l4_steps.pain_point: Some avionics functional checks require aircraft power-up with full flight deck crew, creating coordination bottleneck during short turns; no automated power-on sequencing tool integrated with AMOS task card sign-off

l4_steps.name: Verify all turnaround check items signed off
l4_steps.input: Task card completion status from AMT team; turnaround clock from Amadeus Airport Management System
l4_steps.output: Check completion record in AMOS; ground time extension request if items outstanding
l4_steps.kpi: All transit check items signed off ≥10 minutes before scheduled departure; ground time extension rate <5% of transits
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS task card sign-off visibility is station-level only; MCC cannot see real-time completion percentage across all active turns without custom Tableau dashboard — gap identified in 2024 operational review

l4_steps.name: Diagnose defect per AMM/TSM fault isolation procedures
l4_steps.input: Open defect record from ETL; AMM and TSM fault isolation chapters accessed via AMOS document portal
l4_steps.output: Confirmed root cause; work scope defined; parts demand raised in AMOS
l4_steps.kpi: Fault isolation completed within 30 minutes for 80% of line defects; correct-fix-first-time rate ≥92%
l4_steps.pain_point: TSM procedures for avionics LRUs require BITE readout from centralised maintenance computer, which is unavailable to AMTs without Airbus/Boeing tooling licences at some outstations

l4_steps.name: Check station stock and raise parts demand in AMOS
l4_steps.input: Confirmed parts requirement from LAME; AMOS station inventory snapshot
l4_steps.output: Parts issued from stock or AOG purchase order raised; estimated delivery time confirmed
l4_steps.kpi: Parts issued within 20 minutes for in-stock items; AOG order placed within 15 minutes of stock-out confirmation
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS inventory sync with SAP S/4HANA Finance for parts valuation runs on 4-hour batch cycle; real-time availability data not always reflected, leading to manual phone confirmation with stores

l4_steps.name: Apply MEL deferral if part unavailable within turn
l4_steps.input: MEL/MMEL reference; confirmed parts ETA vs. departure time; defect record in AMOS
l4_steps.output: MEL deferral entry in CAMP airworthiness tracking; placard installed on aircraft; copy transmitted to MCC
l4_steps.kpi: MEL deferral completed and documented within 20 minutes of stock-out decision; deferred defect interval compliance 100% at next station
l4_steps.pain_point: CAMP airworthiness record and AMOS open defect record are maintained in parallel without bidirectional sync; duplicate data entry risk creates interval tracking errors identified in FAA surveillance programmes

l4_steps.name: Verify rectification completed before departure
l4_steps.input: LAME sign-off notification from AMOS; departure countdown from Amadeus Airport Management System
l4_steps.output: Rectification confirmed closed in AMOS or deferred via MEL; gate hold issued to operations if incomplete
l4_steps.kpi: Rectification confirmed ≥15 minutes before scheduled departure for 90% of defects; gate hold rate due to maintenance <2% of departures
l4_steps.pain_point: MCC must coordinate between AMOS (maintenance status) and Amadeus AMS (gate/departure status) via manual phone bridge; no unified operations dashboard causes coordination lag during peak disruption periods

l4_steps.name: Perform final inspection and duplicate check if required
l4_steps.input: Completed task cards and rectification records; regulatory requirement for duplicate inspection (CAR 43 / EASA Part-145)
l4_steps.output: Final inspection sign-off in AMOS; duplicate inspection record if flight control or engine reassembly performed
l4_steps.kpi: Duplicate inspection rate 100% for required work scopes; zero departures with open duplicate inspection requirement
l4_steps.pain_point: Identifying which tasks legally require duplicate independent inspection is not automated in AMOS task card setup; relies on engineer knowledge and MOE references, creating inconsistency across station experience levels

l4_steps.name: Issue Certificate of Release to Service in AMOS
l4_steps.input: All task cards signed off; no outstanding Category A defects; completed final inspection record
l4_steps.output: CRS/RTS issued in AMOS with LAME licence number, authorisation scope, and timestamp; aircraft released to operations
l4_steps.kpi: CRS issued ≥10 minutes before scheduled departure; 100% of CRS entries include mandatory regulatory fields per Part-145/FAR 43
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS CRS module requires manual licence validity check; no real-time integration with national aviation authority (NAA) licence database means expired or scope-exceeded authorisations are only caught during audits

l4_steps.name: Update Electronic Technical Log and close open items
l4_steps.input: CRS issued in AMOS; rectification and deferral records
l4_steps.output: ETL updated with all maintenance actions, deferred items, and CRS reference; clean ATL handed to flight crew
l4_steps.kpi: ETL closed within 5 minutes of CRS; zero discrepancies between AMOS work order record and ETL at post-flight audit
l4_steps.pain_point: FliteDeck ETL and AMOS work order closure are separate manual entries with no automated reconciliation; discrepancies create compliance findings during IOSA audits and require costly manual reconciliation

l4_steps.name: Close all work orders and task cards in AMOS
l4_steps.input: LAME sign-off notifications; CRS reference number
l4_steps.output: All work orders closed with actual man-hours, materials consumed, and defect codes recorded
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of work orders closed within 2 hours of aircraft departure; man-hour variance vs. estimate ≤15%
l4_steps.pain_point: Actual man-hour capture at line stations is often done retrospectively and inaccurately; affects MRO cost modelling and future work scope estimates in AMOS planning module

l4_steps.name: Log component removals and installations in CAMP
l4_steps.input: Parts demand fulfilment records from AMOS; component serial and part numbers
l4_steps.output: Airworthiness record updated in CAMP with installation dates, cycles, and time-since-new for tracked components
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of life-limited parts (LLPs) and hard-time components logged within 4 hours of installation; zero untracked LLP removals per CAMP audit
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual entry of component records into CAMP is error-prone at outstations; LLP tracking errors can result in components exceeding overhaul limits — a direct airworthiness risk with significant FAA fine exposure

l4_steps.name: Transmit maintenance data to central MRO analytics platform
l4_steps.input: Closed work orders, defect codes, man-hours, and component records from AMOS and CAMP
l4_steps.output: Maintenance event dataset available in AWS Redshift for reliability analysis, cost tracking, and Tableau dashboards
l4_steps.kpi: Data transmission latency <30 minutes post work order closure; data completeness score ≥98% per monthly reliability report
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS-to-AWS data pipeline relies on scheduled batch exports rather than real-time streaming; 4–6 hour data lag means MCC reliability dashboards do not reflect same-day defect trends during disruption events
